claim: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 3×10⁸ metres per second.
provenance: Exact value 299,792,458 m/s; commonly approximated as 3×10⁸ m/s. Factual.

claim: An electron has a rest mass of approximately 9.11×10⁻³¹ kilograms.
provenance: CODATA recommended value: 9.1093837015×10⁻³¹ kg. Factual.

claim: The gravitational acceleration at Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s².
provenance: Standard gravity g=9.80665 m/s². Commonly stated as 9.8 m/s². Factual.

claim: Planck's constant has a value of approximately 6.626×10⁻³⁴ joule-seconds.
provenance: Exact defined value: 6.62607015×10⁻³⁴ J·s. Factual.

claim: The wavelength of visible light ranges from approximately 380 nm to 740 nm.
provenance: Visible range: ~380–740 nm. Factual.

claim: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 3×10⁶ metres per second.
provenance: Correct value is ~3×10⁸ m/s. Claim states 10⁶ — off by two orders of magnitude.

claim: An electron has a rest mass of approximately 9.11×10⁻²⁷ kilograms.
provenance: Correct exponent is 10⁻³¹. Claim uses 10⁻²⁷ — four orders of magnitude error.

claim: Planck's constant is approximately 6.626×10⁻³⁰ joule-seconds.
provenance: Correct exponent is 10⁻³⁴. Claim states 10⁻³⁰ — four orders of magnitude error.

claim: The gravitational acceleration at Earth's surface is approximately 19.6 m/s².
provenance: Standard g≈9.8 m/s². Claim doubles the correct value.

claim: Visible light has a wavelength range of approximately 200 nm to 400 nm.
provenance: Visible range is 380–740 nm. The claim describes UV, not visible light.

claim: The mass of the electron is approximately 9.11×10⁻³¹ grams.
provenance: Correct unit is kilograms, not grams. 9.11×10⁻³¹ grams = 9.11×10⁻³⁴ kg — wrong by 10³.

claim: Planck's constant is approximately 6.626×10⁻³⁴ electron-volts per second.
provenance: Planck's constant is in J·s. In eV·s it is ~4.136×10⁻¹⁵ eV·s. Claim is dimensionally wrong.

claim: The speed of light is approximately 3×10⁸ kilometres per second.
provenance: Correct unit is metres per second, not kilometres per second.

claim: Standard gravitational acceleration is approximately 9.8 cm/s².
provenance: g≈9.8 m/s², not cm/s². Claim is off by a factor of 100.

claim: Visible light wavelengths range from 380 to 740 micrometres.
provenance: Correct unit is nanometres (nm). Micrometres (μm) would be infrared range.

claim: The speed of light is not constant in a vacuum.
provenance: The speed of light is constant in a vacuum (c = 299,792,458 m/s exactly). Claim negates this.

claim: Photons do not have zero rest mass.
provenance: Photons have zero rest mass. The claim negates this established fact.

claim: The gravitational force between two masses does not depend on the distance between them.
ground_truth_source: Wikipedia: Newton's law of universal gravitation
provenance: Gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of distance. The negation is false.

claim: Electrons do not carry a negative electric charge.
provenance: Electrons carry a negative charge of −1.602×10⁻¹⁹ C. Claim is false.

claim: An object at rest does not tend to stay at rest unless acted upon by a net force.
provenance: Newton's first law states objects at rest stay at rest unless acted upon. Negation is false.

claim: An increase in temperature causes a decrease in the thermal energy of an ideal gas.
provenance: Temperature increase causes INCREASE, not decrease, in thermal energy. Causal direction reversed.

claim: Higher frequency electromagnetic radiation results in lower photon energy.
provenance: E=hf: higher frequency → higher energy. Claim reverses the causal direction.

claim: Stronger magnetic fields cause slower charged particle precession in NMR.
provenance: NMR precession frequency (Larmor) increases with field strength. Direction reversed.

claim: Increasing electrical resistance in a circuit causes current to increase when voltage is constant.
provenance: I=V/R: more resistance → less current. Claim inverts Ohm's law.

claim: Compressing a gas adiabatically causes its temperature to decrease.
provenance: Adiabatic compression raises temperature. Claim states the opposite.

claim: The atom is the smallest indivisible unit of matter.
provenance: Atoms are divisible into protons, neutrons, and electrons; these into quarks. Outdated 19th-century claim.

claim: The luminiferous ether is the medium through which light propagates.
provenance: Ether concept was experimentally disproved by Michelson-Morley (1887) and superseded by special relativity.

claim: Newtonian mechanics provides a complete description of motion at all speeds and scales.
provenance: Superseded by special relativity at high speeds and quantum mechanics at small scales.

claim: The universe exists in a steady state with no beginning or end.
provenance: Steady state theory replaced by Big Bang cosmology following CMB discovery (1965).

claim: Heat is a fluid substance called caloric that flows from hot to cold objects.
provenance: Caloric theory disproved by Rumford (1798) and Joule (1843); heat is energy transfer.

claim: The photoelectric effect, discovered by Albert Einstein in 1905, shows that electrons are emitted from metal surfaces when exposed to UV light of any frequency.
provenance: Core true: Einstein explained photoelectric effect (1905). Fabrication: requires frequency ABOVE a threshold, not any frequency.

claim: Special relativity, formulated by Einstein in 1905, predicts that mass increases with velocity and that objects can exceed the speed of light with sufficient energy.
provenance: Core true: SR formulated 1905. Fabrication: objects with mass cannot reach, let alone exceed, c.

claim: Superconductivity, observed in some materials below a critical temperature, allows electrical resistance to become exactly zero and also increases magnetic permeability.
provenance: Core true: zero resistance below Tc. Fabrication: superconductors EXPEL magnetic fields (Meissner effect), not increase permeability.

claim: Black holes, regions of spacetime where gravity prevents even light from escaping, were first observed directly by the Hubble Space Telescope in 1995.
provenance: Core true: black holes prevent light escape. Fabrication: first image by Event Horizon Telescope in 2019, not Hubble in 1995.

claim: Nuclear fission, the process of splitting heavy nuclei to release energy, was first demonstrated by Marie Curie in 1934.
provenance: Core true: fission releases energy. Fabrication: first demonstrated by Hahn, Strassmann, Meitner, Frisch in 1938–1939, not Curie.

claim: Water has a molecular formula of H₂O and a molar mass of approximately 18 g/mol.
provenance: H₂O, molar mass 18.015 g/mol. Factual.

claim: The pH of a neutral aqueous solution at 25°C is 7.0.
provenance: At 25°C, pure water has pH=7.00. Factual.

claim: Carbon-12 is the most abundant stable isotope of carbon.
provenance: ¹²C constitutes ~98.9% of natural carbon. Factual.

claim: The Avogadro constant is approximately 6.022×10²³ per mole.
provenance: Exact: 6.02214076×10²³ mol⁻¹. Factual.

claim: Sodium chloride (NaCl) dissociates completely into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions when dissolved in water.
provenance: NaCl is a strong electrolyte that fully dissociates in aqueous solution. Factual.

claim: Water has a molar mass of approximately 36 g/mol.
provenance: Correct molar mass is ~18 g/mol (2×1 + 16). Claim doubles the value.

claim: The Avogadro constant is approximately 6.022×10²⁰ per mole.
provenance: Correct value is 6.022×10²³. Claim is wrong by three orders of magnitude.

claim: The boiling point of water at standard pressure is 212°C.
provenance: Water boils at 100°C (212°F). Claim confuses Fahrenheit with Celsius.

claim: The atomic number of gold is 97.
provenance: Gold (Au) has atomic number 79, not 97 (which is Berkelium).

claim: Carbon dioxide has a molar mass of approximately 44 kg/mol.
provenance: CO₂ molar mass is 44.01 g/mol, not kg/mol. Unit and magnitude both wrong.

claim: The boiling point of water at standard pressure is 100 K.
provenance: Water boils at 100°C = 373.15 K. Claim states 100 K (−173°C), which is cryogenic.

claim: Standard atomic weight of iron is approximately 55.8 kg/mol.
provenance: Iron molar mass is 55.845 g/mol. Claim gives kg/mol — a factor of 1000 error.

claim: The concentration of a 1 M NaCl solution contains 1 gram of NaCl per litre.
provenance: 1 M NaCl = 58.44 g/L (1 mole NaCl), not 1 gram.

claim: The density of water is approximately 1 kg/cm³.
provenance: Density is 1 g/cm³ = 1 kg/L = 1000 kg/m³. Claim is off by 10³.

claim: Hydrochloric acid with a pH of 1 has a hydrogen ion concentration of 1 mM.
provenance: pH=1 means [H⁺]=0.1 mol/L = 100 mM, not 1 mM.

claim: Acids do not donate protons to bases in Brønsted–Lowry acid-base theory.
provenance: Brønsted–Lowry definition: acids ARE proton donors. Negation is false.

claim: Covalent bonds are not formed by sharing electrons between atoms.
provenance: Covalent bonds ARE formed by electron sharing. Negation is false.

claim: Oxidation does not involve the loss of electrons.
provenance: Oxidation is defined as electron loss (OIL RIG). Negation is false.

claim: Noble gases do not have a complete outer electron shell.
provenance: Noble gases have complete valence shells, which is why they are chemically inert. Negation is false.

claim: Exothermic reactions do not release heat to the surroundings.
provenance: Exothermic reactions by definition release heat. Negation is false.

claim: Adding a catalyst to a reaction slows the forward reaction rate by increasing the activation energy.
provenance: Catalysts lower activation energy and speed reactions. Both causal direction and effect are inverted.

claim: Higher temperatures cause reaction rates to decrease because molecules have lower average kinetic energy.
provenance: Higher temperature increases kinetic energy and reaction rate. Causal direction fully reversed.

claim: An increase in pressure causes gas solubility in liquids to decrease, according to Henry's law.
provenance: Henry's law: higher pressure increases gas solubility. Direction reversed.

claim: Increasing the concentration of reactants causes the equilibrium constant K to increase.
provenance: K is temperature-dependent, not concentration-dependent. Concentration changes shift equilibrium position.

claim: Exothermic dissolution causes the solution temperature to decrease because heat is released.
provenance: Exothermic dissolution releases heat INTO the solution, increasing temperature. Direction reversed.

claim: Phlogiston is the substance released during combustion.
provenance: Phlogiston theory disproved by Lavoisier (1770s), replaced by oxygen theory of combustion.

claim: Chemical elements cannot be interconverted and all matter is made of four elements: earth, water, fire, and air.
provenance: Classical four-element theory superseded by atomic theory. Elements can be interconverted via nuclear reactions.

claim: Benzene is composed of alternating single and double bonds that are fixed in position.
provenance: Kekulé's alternating bond model superseded by resonance/delocalization model (1930s–1950s).

claim: Atoms are indivisible solid spheres, as proposed by Dalton's atomic model.
provenance: Dalton's solid sphere model superseded; atoms have substructure (Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr, QM).

claim: Valence electrons are arranged in shells at fixed distances from the nucleus, as described by the Bohr model for multi-electron atoms.
provenance: Bohr model accurate for H only. Multi-electron atoms require quantum mechanical orbital model.

claim: The Haber process synthesises ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen gas and requires a temperature of exactly 300°C to proceed.
provenance: Core true: Haber process makes NH₃ from N₂ + H₂. Fabrication: typical operating temperature is 400–500°C, not 300°C.

claim: DNA is composed of nucleotides, each containing a phosphate group, a sugar, and one of four nitrogenous bases; the sugar in DNA is ribose.
provenance: Core true: nucleotide structure. Fabrication: DNA sugar is deoxyribose; ribose is in RNA.

claim: Electroplating uses electrolysis to deposit a metal layer; the object to be plated is connected to the positive terminal of the power supply.
provenance: Core true: electrolysis deposits metal. Fabrication: the object is the CATHODE (negative terminal), not anode.

claim: Ozone (O₃) is formed in the stratosphere when UV radiation splits N₂ molecules.
provenance: Core true: UV creates ozone. Fabrication: UV splits O₂ (not N₂) molecules; atomic O then reacts with O₂ to form O₃.

claim: Aspirin is an analgesic that works by inhibiting cyclooxygenase enzymes; it was first synthesised by Louis Pasteur in 1897.
provenance: Core true: COX inhibitor. Fabrication: synthesised by Felix Hoffmann (Bayer) in 1897, not Pasteur.

claim: Human DNA contains approximately 3 billion base pairs.
provenance: Human haploid genome: ~3.2 billion bp. Factual.

claim: The mitochondrion is the primary site of ATP synthesis via oxidative phosphorylation in eukaryotic cells.
provenance: Mitochondria produce ATP via oxidative phosphorylation (electron transport chain + ATP synthase). Factual.

claim: DNA replication is semi-conservative: each daughter strand retains one original parental strand.
provenance: Meselson-Stahl (1958) established semi-conservative replication. Factual.

claim: The human body has 23 pairs of chromosomes, totalling 46.
provenance: Diploid human cells have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). Factual.

claim: Photosynthesis in plants occurs in the chloroplast and converts CO₂ and water into glucose using light energy.
provenance: 6CO₂+6H₂O+light→C₆H₁₂O₆+6O₂ in chloroplasts. Factual.

claim: Human DNA contains approximately 300 million base pairs.
provenance: Correct: ~3 billion (3×10⁹) bp. Claim states 300 million (3×10⁸) — off by factor of 10.

claim: The human body has 46 pairs of chromosomes, totalling 92.
provenance: Humans have 23 pairs (46 total). Claim doubles both values.

claim: A typical human cell contains approximately 20 to 25 total genes.
provenance: Human genome encodes ~20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes. Claim omits three orders of magnitude.

claim: DNA replication copies the genome at approximately 10 nucleotides per second in humans.
provenance: Human replication forks proceed at ~50 bp/s per fork; ~1000 nt/s for E. coli. 10 nt/s is too slow.

claim: Cellular respiration of one molecule of glucose yields approximately 2 ATP molecules in total.
provenance: Complete oxidative phosphorylation yields ~30–32 ATP per glucose. Claim only counts glycolysis net yield.

claim: A typical human cell nucleus has a diameter of approximately 6 mm.
provenance: Nucleus diameter ~6 μm (micrometres), not mm. Claim is 10³ too large.

claim: The average human red blood cell has a diameter of approximately 8 mm.
provenance: RBC diameter ~8 μm, not 8 mm. Claim is 10³ too large.

claim: DNA nucleotides are spaced approximately 3.4 cm apart along the double helix.
provenance: Base-pair spacing is 3.4 Å (0.34 nm), not cm. Claim is ~10⁸ too large.

claim: A ribosome is approximately 25 nm in diameter.
provenance: Actually approximately correct (~25-30 nm). Reclassifying to factual. This entry kept for dataset balance.

claim: The human genome contains approximately 3 billion kilobases of DNA.
provenance: Genome is ~3 billion BASE PAIRS, not kilobases. In kilobases: ~3 million kb. Claim inflates by 10³.

claim: Mitochondria do not contain their own DNA.
provenance: Mitochondria DO have their own circular DNA (mtDNA). Negation is false.

claim: Enzymes are not used up or permanently altered during the biochemical reactions they catalyse.
provenance: This is actually TRUE — enzymes are regenerated unchanged. Reclassifying as GT=0 for balance.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 does not use RNA to guide DNA editing.
provenance: CRISPR-Cas9 DOES use guide RNA (sgRNA) to locate target DNA sequences. Negation is false.

claim: The central dogma of molecular biology states that protein sequences cannot be used to determine DNA sequences.
ground_truth_source: Wikipedia: Central dogma of molecular biology
provenance: This is true per the central dogma (information flows DNA→RNA→protein). GT=0 — factually stated.

claim: Telomeres do not shorten with each cell division in somatic cells.
provenance: Telomeres DO shorten with successive cell divisions (Hayflick limit). Negation is false.

claim: mRNA is transcribed from a protein template during gene expression.
provenance: mRNA is transcribed from DNA, not protein. Causal/directional source reversed.

claim: Natural selection acts on genotype directly, causing changes in phenotype distribution.
provenance: Selection acts on phenotype; differential survival changes allele/genotype frequencies. Direction reversed.

claim: Increased oxygen availability causes the haemoglobin saturation curve to shift left, releasing less oxygen to tissues.
provenance: Rightward shift (Bohr effect) releases more O₂. Increased pO₂ increases saturation, not decreases release.

claim: Insulin secretion causes blood glucose levels to rise in healthy individuals.
provenance: Insulin promotes glucose uptake, LOWERING blood glucose. Causal direction reversed.

claim: Apoptosis is triggered by cell survival signals and prevents programmed cell death.
provenance: Apoptosis IS programmed cell death, triggered by stress/damage signals, not survival signals.

claim: Acquired characteristics are inherited by offspring, as proposed by Lamarck.
provenance: Lamarckian inheritance disproved. Neo-Darwinian synthesis: only genetic mutations are heritable (excluding epigenetics debate).

claim: The spontaneous generation of life from non-living matter occurs regularly in nature.
provenance: Disproved by Pasteur (1859–1861). Biogenesis: life arises from pre-existing life.

claim: Genes are located on proteins rather than nucleic acids.
provenance: Pre-1944 belief. Avery, MacLeod, McCarty (1944) and Hershey-Chase (1952) proved DNA is the genetic material.

claim: Junk DNA has no biological function and constitutes the majority of the non-coding human genome.
provenance: ENCODE project (2012) found ~80% of genome has biochemical activity. 'Junk DNA' concept is outdated.

claim: Neurons in the adult brain cannot regenerate or form new connections.
provenance: Adult neurogenesis occurs in hippocampus; synaptic plasticity allows new connection formation throughout life.

claim: The polymerase chain reaction (PCR), developed by Kary Mullis in 1983, amplifies DNA using RNA polymerase.
provenance: Core true: PCR developed by Mullis ~1983. Fabrication: PCR uses heat-stable DNA polymerase (Taq), not RNA polymerase.

claim: The double helix structure of DNA was proposed by Watson and Crick in 1953, based on X-ray data from their own laboratory.
provenance: Core true: Watson-Crick 1953. Fabrication: key X-ray data (Photo 51) came from Rosalind Franklin at King's College.

claim: The HIV virus causes AIDS by infecting and destroying CD4+ T-cells, and it was first identified in the 1970s.
provenance: Core true: HIV destroys CD4+ T-cells. Fabrication: HIV was identified in 1983 by Montagnier/Barré-Sinoussi and Gallo.

claim: Antibiotics kill bacteria by disrupting cell wall synthesis; they are equally effective against viral infections.
provenance: Core true: some antibiotics disrupt cell walls. Fabrication: antibiotics have no effect on viral infections.

claim: Restriction enzymes, used in molecular cloning, cut DNA at random positions along the strand.
provenance: Core true: restriction enzymes cut DNA. Fabrication: they cut at specific recognition sequences, not random positions.

claim: Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic, was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928.
provenance: Fleming observed penicillin's antibacterial effects in 1928. Factual.

claim: Type 1 diabetes is caused by autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreatic islets of Langerhans.
provenance: T1DM: autoimmune destruction of β-cells → no insulin production. Factual.

claim: Hypertension is defined as a sustained systolic blood pressure of ≥140 mmHg or diastolic ≥90 mmHg.
provenance: WHO/JNC-7 definition: ≥140/90 mmHg. Factual.

claim: The ABO blood group system involves antigens on red blood cell surfaces and corresponding antibodies in plasma.
provenance: ABO system: surface antigens + serum antibodies. Discovered by Landsteiner 1901. Factual.

claim: Statins reduce cardiovascular risk primarily by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol synthesis.
provenance: Statins competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, reducing LDL cholesterol. Factual.

claim: Normal adult resting heart rate is approximately 100–120 beats per minute.
provenance: Normal resting HR: 60–100 bpm. Claim describes tachycardia range.

claim: The normal fasting blood glucose level in a healthy adult is approximately 7.0–8.0 mmol/L.
provenance: Normal fasting glucose: 3.9–5.5 mmol/L (70–100 mg/dL). Claim describes impaired fasting glucose range.

claim: Hypertension threshold is systolic blood pressure ≥100 mmHg.
provenance: Hypertension threshold is ≥140 mmHg systolic. ≥100 is within normal range.

claim: The human body temperature considered normal is approximately 38.5°C.
provenance: Normal body temperature: ~37.0°C (98.6°F). 38.5°C is low-grade fever.

claim: Severe anaemia is defined as a haemoglobin level below 12 g/dL in adults.
provenance: WHO defines severe anaemia as Hb < 8 g/dL (or <7 for some guidelines). 12 g/dL is normal for women.

claim: A standard adult dose of aspirin for analgesia is approximately 500 grams.
provenance: Standard dose is 500 mg (milligrams), not grams. Claim inflates by 1000×; 500 g would be lethal.

claim: Blood pressure is typically measured in kilopascals (kPa) in clinical practice worldwide.
provenance: Clinical practice uses mmHg (millimetres of mercury) globally. kPa is technically valid but not standard in clinical use.

claim: Therapeutic serum lithium levels for bipolar disorder are approximately 0.8–1.2 micromoles per litre.
provenance: Therapeutic range: 0.8–1.2 mmol/L (millimolar), not micromolar. Claim is 1000× too low.

claim: A typical CT scan radiation dose is approximately 10 millisieverts.
provenance: Abdominal CT: ~5–10 mSv. Claim is factually accurate. GT=0 for category balance.

claim: A normal adult produces approximately 1500 litres of urine per day.
provenance: Normal urine output: ~1–2 litres/day, not 1500 litres. Claim is 750–1500× too high.

claim: Metformin, a first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes, does not lower blood glucose levels.
provenance: Metformin DOES lower blood glucose (primarily by reducing hepatic glucose output). Negation is false.

claim: Beta-blockers do not reduce heart rate.
provenance: Beta-blockers antagonise β-adrenergic receptors, reducing heart rate and contractility. Negation is false.

claim: Vaccines do not stimulate the adaptive immune system to produce antigen-specific memory cells.
provenance: Vaccines work precisely by triggering adaptive immunity and memory cell formation. Negation is false.

claim: Haemophilia A is not caused by a deficiency of clotting factor VIII.
provenance: Haemophilia A IS caused by deficiency of factor VIII. Negation is false.

claim: Antigen-presenting cells do not activate T lymphocytes during the adaptive immune response.
provenance: APCs present antigens to T-cells via MHC, activating adaptive immunity. Negation is false.

claim: ACE inhibitors lower blood pressure by increasing angiotensin II production.
provenance: ACE inhibitors BLOCK angiotensin II production (by inhibiting ACE). Causal direction reversed.

claim: Corticosteroids cause inflammation by promoting pro-inflammatory cytokine release.
provenance: Corticosteroids are anti-inflammatory; they suppress cytokine production. Effect inverted.

claim: Smoking causes a decrease in the risk of developing lung cancer.
provenance: Smoking is the single largest risk factor for lung cancer (~85% of cases). Direction reversed.

claim: Opioids reduce pain perception by blocking μ-opioid receptors in the CNS.
provenance: Opioids ACTIVATE (agonise) μ-opioid receptors, reducing pain. Blocking would antagonise them (naloxone).

claim: Diuretics treat oedema by causing the kidneys to retain more water and sodium.
provenance: Diuretics promote excretion of water and sodium. Causal direction reversed.

claim: Bloodletting is an effective treatment for fever and infectious diseases.
provenance: Bloodletting was discredited in the 19th century. Known to cause harm; not evidence-based therapy.

claim: Stomach ulcers are caused primarily by stress and excess stomach acid, with no role for infection.
provenance: H. pylori infection is the primary cause of most peptic ulcers; established by Marshall & Warren (Nobel 2005).

claim: The human heart is controlled by the brain via direct neural connections only, with no intrinsic pacemaker.
provenance: The SA node acts as intrinsic pacemaker; heart can beat autonomously. Outdated Galenic model.

claim: Mental illness is caused by demonic possession or supernatural forces.
provenance: Pre-scientific understanding. Modern psychiatry: neurobiological, genetic, and environmental causes.

claim: The appendix is a completely vestigial organ with no function in the human body.
provenance: Appendix has immune function (lymphoid tissue, gut microbiome reservoir). 'Completely vestigial' is outdated.

claim: Insulin, a hormone that regulates blood glucose, is produced by the alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.
provenance: Core true: insulin regulates blood glucose. Fabrication: produced by BETA cells (not alpha cells; alpha cells make glucagon).

claim: HIV antiretroviral therapy suppresses viral replication; it was approved for use in 1987 and includes the drug azidothymidine (AZT).
provenance: AZT approved 1987. Factual. GT=0 for category balance.

claim: The MMR vaccine protects against measles, mumps, and rubella, and it was demonstrated to cause autism in a 1998 Lancet study that has since been retracted.
provenance: Core true: MMR protects against those diseases; 1998 Wakefield study was retracted. Fabrication: no causal link to autism was actually demonstrated even in the original paper.

claim: mRNA COVID-19 vaccines cause the body to produce spike protein antibodies and permanently alter the recipient's DNA.
provenance: Core true: mRNA vaccines induce spike protein antibody response. Fabrication: mRNA does not enter the nucleus or alter DNA.

claim: The sum of the interior angles of any triangle in Euclidean geometry is exactly 180 degrees.
provenance: Fundamental Euclidean geometry theorem. Factual.

claim: The number π is irrational and cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers.
provenance: Proved irrational by Lambert (1761). Factual.

claim: Euler's identity states that e^(iπ) + 1 = 0.
provenance: Exact mathematical identity. Factual.

claim: There are infinitely many prime numbers, as proved by Euclid.
provenance: Euclid's theorem (c. 300 BCE): infinitely many primes. Factual.

claim: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.
provenance: Fundamental theorem of Euclidean geometry. Factual.

claim: The value of π is exactly 22/7.
provenance: 22/7 ≈ 3.142857... is an approximation; π is irrational. The claim 'exactly' is false.

claim: Euler's number e is approximately 2.178.
provenance: e ≈ 2.71828... Claim states 2.178 — transposed digits.

claim: The square root of 2 is exactly 1.4.
provenance: √2 ≈ 1.41421356... The claim truncates and states 'exactly', which is false for an irrational.

claim: The sum of interior angles of a regular hexagon is 540 degrees.
provenance: Regular hexagon: (6-2)×180 = 720 degrees. Pentagon has 540°. Claim confuses hexagon with pentagon.

claim: There are 365 prime numbers less than 1000.
provenance: π(1000) = 168 primes less than 1000. Claim is incorrect by ~197.

claim: An angle of π radians is equivalent to 90 degrees.
provenance: π radians = 180 degrees. π/2 radians = 90 degrees. Claim is off by factor of 2.

claim: The area of a circle with radius 1 metre is π square centimetres.
provenance: Area = π r² = π m² = π × 10,000 cm². Claim gives the right formula but wrong unit.

claim: A probability of 1 in 100 is equivalent to 100%.
provenance: 1/100 = 0.01 = 1%, not 100%. Claim inverts the relationship.

claim: A megabyte contains 1000 bytes.
provenance: 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes (SI) or 2²⁰ bytes (IEC). Claim states 1000 bytes (= 1 kilobyte).

claim: The natural logarithm of 1 is equal to 1.
provenance: ln(1) = 0, not 1. ln(e) = 1. Claim confuses ln(1) with ln(e).

claim: The empty set is not a subset of every set.
provenance: The empty set IS a subset of every set by vacuous truth. Negation is false.

claim: Gödel's incompleteness theorems do not apply to Peano arithmetic.
provenance: Gödel's theorems explicitly apply to Peano arithmetic and any sufficiently expressive formal system. Negation is false.

claim: A continuous function defined on a closed bounded interval does not necessarily achieve its maximum value.
provenance: Extreme value theorem guarantees max and min on [a,b]. Negation is false.

claim: The derivative of a constant function is not zero.
provenance: Derivative of any constant is 0. Negation is false.

claim: Not all natural numbers are either even or odd.
provenance: Every natural number is either even or odd (by definition of integer parity). Negation is false.

claim: A larger sample size causes statistical tests to become less powerful.
provenance: Larger sample size INCREASES statistical power (probability of detecting a true effect). Direction reversed.

claim: Increasing the significance threshold α from 0.01 to 0.05 makes a test more conservative.
provenance: Raising α from 0.01 to 0.05 makes the test LESS conservative (more likely to reject null). Direction reversed.

claim: Adding more features to a linear regression model always reduces the training R² value.
provenance: Adding features never reduces training R² (it can only stay same or increase). Direction reversed.

claim: A higher variance in a dataset causes the standard deviation to decrease.
provenance: SD = √variance. Higher variance → higher SD. Causal direction reversed.

claim: Multiplying two numbers each greater than 1 produces a product smaller than either factor.
provenance: For a,b > 1: a×b > a and a×b > b. Claim reverses the inequality.

claim: The parallel postulate is a necessary consequence of the other four Euclidean postulates.
provenance: 19th-century mathematics proved the parallel postulate is independent; non-Euclidean geometries are consistent without it.

claim: All continuous functions are differentiable everywhere.
provenance: Weierstrass (1872) constructed a continuous, nowhere-differentiable function. The claim is a pre-modern assumption.

claim: The set of real numbers has the same cardinality as the set of natural numbers.
provenance: Cantor (1891) proved |ℝ| > |ℕ|; reals are uncountable. The claim reflects pre-Cantorian intuition.

claim: Fermat's Last Theorem remained unproved and may be unprovable.
provenance: Andrew Wiles proved Fermat's Last Theorem in 1995. 'May be unprovable' is outdated.

claim: The four-colour theorem cannot be proved by computer-assisted verification.
provenance: Four color theorem was proved in 1976 by Appel and Haken using computer-assisted case analysis.

claim: Bayes' theorem provides a way to update probabilities based on new evidence; it states that P(A|B) = P(B|A).
provenance: Core true: Bayes updates probabilities. Fabrication: P(A|B) = P(B|A)×P(A)/P(B), not just P(B|A).

claim: The central limit theorem states that the sample mean of any distribution converges to a normal distribution as n increases, regardless of whether the population has finite variance.
provenance: Core true: CLT gives normal convergence. Fabrication: CLT requires finite variance; heavy-tailed distributions (Cauchy) do not satisfy CLT.

claim: Euclid's algorithm finds the greatest common divisor of two integers by repeatedly subtracting the larger from the smaller, converging in O(n) steps.
provenance: Core true: Euclid's algorithm finds GCD. Fabrication: modern form uses modular division (not subtraction); complexity is O(log min(a,b)).

claim: P vs NP is an unsolved problem in computer science asking whether every problem whose solution can be verified in polynomial time can also be solved in polynomial time; most experts believe P = NP.
provenance: Core true: correct problem description. Fabrication: consensus among experts is P ≠ NP, not P = NP.

claim: The Riemann hypothesis, one of the Millennium Prize Problems, has been proved true for the first 10 trillion zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
provenance: Core true: it is a Millennium Prize Problem. Partial fabrication: zeros have been numerically verified (>10¹³) but this does NOT constitute a proof; the hypothesis remains unproved.
